patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Episode of acute upper abdominal pain treated three years ago. History of long-term alcohol consumption and smoking.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Stopped alcohol consumption three years ago; 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

objective_for_doctor: Assess the patient and determine the cause of jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stool, and dark urine.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Over the last two weeks my skin has gradually turned yellow, and I’ve had generalized itching. I’m also not eating well and I’ve lost about 6.3 kg, with pale stools and very dark urine.
Are you experiencing any abdominal pain or discomfort?
I haven’t had significant abdominal pain recently, but I do notice my appetite is down. No new severe discomfort—just the yellowing of my skin, itching, pale stools, and dark urine.
Have you had any fevers, chills, or night sweats recently?
“No, I haven’t had fevers, chills, or night sweats. It’s mainly been the yellow skin, itching, dark urine, pale stools, and the drop in appetite and weight.”
How old are you, and do you have any past medical conditions or take any medications regularly?
I’m 72 years old. I don’t take any regular medications, but about three years ago I had an acute upper abdominal pain episode that was treated with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary changes.
Do you smoke tobacco or drink alcohol, and do you have any family history of cancer?

“I do smoke—about a pack a day for many years—and I stopped alcohol about three years ago; I’d been having 1–2 beers daily before then. As for family history of cancer, I don’t recall any major cancer in close relatives.”

I haven’t noticed increased thirst or frequent urination. I’m mainly dealing with the progressive yellow skin, generalized itching, poor appetite with weight loss, pale stools, and very dark urine. No fevers, chills, or night sweats either.

Patient: I haven’t noticed any swelling in my legs, and no noticeable swelling elsewhere. It’s mostly the gradual yellow skin, the generalized itching, and the changes in stool and urine—pale stools and very dark urine—along with poor appetite and the weight loss.

Patient: No, I’ve never been told I have gallstones. I did have that upper abdominal pain episode three years ago, but since then it was mostly resolved and I’ve only noticed these new changes over the last two weeks.

Patient: No significant nausea or vomiting, and I haven’t had a persistent feeling of being sick—my main issues have been the gradual yellowing, generalized itching, pale stools, very dark urine, and the reduced appetite with weight loss.

“No, I haven’t felt any obvious mass or fullness, and I haven’t noticed any enlarging swelling—just the progressive yellow skin with generalized itching, pale stools, very dark urine, and the drop in appetite with weight loss.”
